pictures.author: Dosseman
pictures.observations: Entire960x640 picture inspected. Tall pale ashlar long wall with worn uneven crest and moulded base, narrow arched window openings, open steel bracing over its rear half. Lower perpendicular vestibule wall and partly obscured portal area near the mosque/tree. Loose foreground stone/drum fragments. No intact ancient roof.

pictures.author: 𐰇𐰱𐰚𐰣
pictures.observations: Entire960x720 current rear oblique inspected. Two tall open cella walls, steel frame above/beside the wall and arched openings, lower irregular stone remnants with multiple thin red brick bands at the rear, low parallel exposed foundations and scattered stone blocks. Modern mosque stands immediately alongside; no surveyed hidden-room or conservation frame inventory inferred.

pictures.author: StefanC
pictures.observations: Entire960x643 close view inspected. Pale ashlar vestibule surfaces and smoother worn inscription field with irregular shallow sockets/pitting; a tree obscures the portal, so this picture does not establish the doorway silhouette. Exact readable text and individually copied damage are omitted.

pictures.author: Klaus-Peter Simon
pictures.observations: Entire960x646 wider south view inspected to resolve the doorway hidden in the other front views. Very tall open rectangular portal with layered jambs and projecting carved lintel under a surviving crosswall; open vestibule, long ashlar wall and arched windows, steel bracing visible through the portal, scattered broken drums and low foundations. Broad portal trim is original simplified geometry, not copied sculptural/text detail.

currentRoundInspection.scope: Surviving open temple ruins inside the mapped Ankara archaeological site: two tall broken limestone cella walls, southwest open vestibule, tall genuine rectangular portal with layered jambs/lintel, three small arched window openings in the southeast wall, low rear stone/brick-banded remnants, scattered foundations and broken drums, plus an open modern steel conservation frame. No ancient roof, pediment or complete colonnade is restored. Internal dimensions and remnant/frame inventory are picture-led approximations; the neighboring mosque is independent native context.
